question: How many officials are there for looking after each Kabaddi match?
solution:
The correct answer is __**6**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• In Kabaddi, a typical match is overseen by **6 officials** who ensure that the game is conducted fairly and according to the rules.

• These officials include one referee, two umpires, a scorer, and two assistant scorers.

• The referee has the final authority on all decisions and is responsible for the overall conduct of the game.

• The umpires assist the referee and are responsible for judging points, fouls, and other infractions during the game.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Roles of Kabaddi Officials**

• **Referee:** The referee is the chief official of the game and has the ultimate authority in all decisions related to the game. The referee's role includes starting and stopping the game, ensuring the rules are followed, and making decisions on contentious issues.

• **Umpires:** There are two umpires in a Kabaddi match who assist the referee. They are responsible for observing the game and making decisions on points, fouls, and other infractions. The umpires work in coordination with the referee to ensure fair play.

• **Scorer:** The scorer is responsible for keeping track of the score, recording points, and maintaining the official score sheet. The scorer ensures that the score is accurately reflected on the scorecard.

• **Assistant Scorers:** There are two assistant scorers who help the main scorer in maintaining the score sheet. They also keep track of the timing, substitutions, and other administrative tasks during the match.

• **Kabaddi Game Overview:**

• Kabaddi is a contact team sport that originated in India. It is played between two teams of seven players each.

• The objective of the game is for a single player on offense, referred to as a "raider," to run into the opposing team's half, tag as many of their players as possible, and return to their own half without being tackled by the defenders.

• Points are scored for each player tagged, and the defending team earns points for stopping the raider.

• The game is played on a rectangular court, and each half lasts for 20 minutes with a 5-minute break in between.

• Kabaddi requires a combination of strength, strategy, and agility, making it an exciting and dynamic sport.
